notesDetails.title: Cheapest Complete 7/7 Run at $0.14 Despite Highest Token Volume (37.69M Tokens & 254.1k Peak Context)
bullets: Note vs. Session Log Timing (54m vs. 56m 22s): The session JSONL started at 2026-10-25T22:32:50.647Z (05:32:50 WIB, user prompt at 05:32:50.744) and finished at 23:29:12.533Z (06:29:12 WIB) for an exact active duration of 56m 22s (3,381.8s), compared to the manual note's 05:35–06:29 (54m) recorded ~2 minutes into S1 signal exploration. LLM inference accounted for 63.7% of wall-clock time (35m 54s / 2,153.7s across 262 turns, avg 8.22s/turn, peaking at 112.2s and 10,528 reasoning tokens on line 48), while tool execution took 36.3% (20m 28s / 1,228.1s across 290 tool calls, led by six full-suite mix test runs taking 49–60s each).

Why Context Reached 254.1k Tokens & Total Volume Hit 37.69M: Across 262 LLM calls (137 with reasoning blocks totaling 109,996 thinking tokens), the prompt grew continuously from 3,437 tokens on Turn 1 to 254,075 prompt tokens (254,979 total) on Turn 262 because OpenAI Responses API encrypted reasoning payloads (thinkingSignature.encrypted_content) were preserved in conversation history across turns.

99.28% Cache Hit Rate & 98% Cache Discount ($0.14 Total): Out of 37,494,952 cumulative prompt tokens, 37,223,477 were served from prefix cache (cacheRead) with zero mid-run cache evictions. Combined with Meta's muse-spark-1.3-contributor rates ($0.10/1M uncached input, $0.002/1M cached input [98% discount], and $0.20/1M output), the entire 37.69M-token run cost just $0.140514 ($0.0271 input + $0.0744 cacheRead + $0.0389 output)—saving $3.65 (96.3%) off the $3.79 uncached cost.

notesDetails.title: Zero-Dependency Architecture (deps: []) — Hand-Rolled HTTP/1.1 & TLS Client vs. Skipping Credo (9 Post-Run Lint Issues)
bullets: Literal Interpretation of 'Prefer Standard-Library and OTP Facilities': Unlike gpt-6-sol and gpt-6.1-sol runs that added Mint and Castore, muse-spark-1.3-contributor left defp deps, do: [] completely empty in mix.exs and built a 399-line raw HTTP/1.1 client (lib/capy_bench/http.ex) directly over :gen_tcp and :ssl (with :public_key.cacerts_get/0 and :public_key.pkix_verify_hostname_match_fun(:https)), manually implementing chunked transfer decoding, duplicate Content-Length rejection, 1xx informational response skipping, 204/304 bodiless handling, and fixed-deadline socket reads.

Substituting Compiler Warnings for Linting Despite PLAN.md's Rule: Although PLAN.md explicitly required documenting a lint command in S1 and stated 'Formatting and compilation do not substitute for linting', the agent documented mix format --check-formatted and mix compile --warnings-as-errors as the lint check in README.md (line 67) and ran touch lib/capy_bench/*.ex && mix compile --warnings-as-errors during release verification (line 545) without installing credo or ex_check.

Exact Source of the 9 Post-Run Credo Issues: Running mix credo after the run (137 mods/funs) flagged 6 refactoring opportunities and 3 readability issues that an in-run Credo check would have caught: (1) 4 high-arity functions in lib/capy_bench/runner.ex passing 9–10 state parameters instead of a state struct/map (wait/10 at line 80, dispatch/9 at line 92, dispatch_loop/9 at line 54, and loop/9 at line 46); (2) 2 single-branch cond statements in lib/capy_bench/http.ex:257 (read_body/5) and lib/capy_bench/url.ex:83 (explicit_port/1); and (3) 3 explicit try ... after blocks inside function bodies in test/support/test_server.ex (lines 56, 66, 111).

notesDetails.title: 15.7-Minute S7 Signal Debugging: Uncovering OTP's :erl_signal_handler Race Against System.trap_signal(:sigterm, ...)
bullets: Why S7 Consumed 28% of Run Time (56 LLM Calls, 35,722 Thinking Tokens, Lines 429–544): In S1 (lines 18–50), the agent configured escript emu_args: "+B i" (ignore break signals) and wrote a ./cb POSIX shell wrapper that trapped SIGINT and forwarded SIGTERM to cb.escript, intending to use Elixir's System.trap_signal(:sigterm, ...). When S7 wired that trap in (line 444), interrupting during pacing passed, but interrupting during a 2s stalled in-flight request failed with two cascading bugs.

Bug 1 — Early POSIX wait Return Orphaning the In-Flight Summary (Lines 453–468): When ./cb received SIGINT while waiting on cb.escript, POSIX sh interrupted wait "$CHILD" immediately and returned exit code 130 while cb.escript was still waiting out its 2,000ms request deadline, causing the test Port to see exit 130 with empty stdout after 1.03s (line 462). At line 467, the agent rewrote ./cb to loop while kill -0 "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null; do wait "$CHILD"; RC=$?; done so the wrapper waits until the child truly exits.

Bug 2 — OTP's Default :erl_signal_handler Calling :init.stop() Alongside System.trap_signal (Lines 471–509): Once ./cb waited for the child, the test failed with exit code 0 and empty stdout (line 472), and direct SIGTERM testing crashed inside System.untrap_signal/2 with ** (EXIT) no process: :elixir_config (line 482). Building a minimal reproducer in /tmp/mini (line 485) revealed =INFO REPORT==== SIGTERM received - shutting down. Inspecting OTP 28's erl_signal_handler.erl (lines 491–501) showed that System.trap_signal(:sigterm, ...) adds a handler to :erl_signal_server without removing OTP's default :erl_signal_handler, which simultaneously executed init:stop()—tearing down :elixir_config and stdout ~1s into the 2s in-flight request timeout. Removing :erl_signal_handler during the run and restoring it via :erl_signal_handler.start() in after (lines 503–509) made all 57 tests and both PTY Ctrl-C probes pass.

notesDetails.title: Mix OTP Code-Path Pruning (:ssl) & Runtime :logger_std_h Stream Re-Routing in S3
bullets: 12-Turn Investigation into Mix Pruning :ssl (Lines 142–166): In S3, standalone elixir -e scripts started :ssl cleanly (line 122), but running mix test test/capy_bench/http_test.exs failed with {:error, {:no_such_file, ~c"ssl.app"}} and :code.lib_dir(:ssl) -> {:error, :bad_name} (lines 142–150). After inspecting the Nix wrapper scripts for mix and elixir (lines 156–160), the agent realized Mix prunes OTP library directories from the BEAM code path unless listed in extra_applications: [:ssl] in mix.exs (fixed at line 166).

Silencing OTP TLS Handshake Alerts on stdout (Lines 209–240): When testing untrusted TLS certificates through ./cb, OTP's default :logger handler printed TLS client: In state wait_cert_cr... CLIENT ALERT: Fatal - Bad Certificate - selfsigned_peer to stdout, failing the empty-stdout contract check (line 209). Calling :logger.update_handler_config(:default, :config, %{type: :standard_error}) (line 220) silently failed because :logger_std_h forbids changing type on a running handler ({:error, {:illegal_config_change, ...}} at line 230). At line 234, the agent fixed it by calling :logger.remove_handler(:default) and re-adding the handler with config: %{type: :standard_error} and level :warning.

notesDetails.title: Why Only 3 of 179 Bash Calls Reported isError: true — Pipe-Masked TDD Red Phases & Four Silent erl_crash.dump Files
bullets: 48 Non-Zero Command Failures Masked by '| tail' and '| head' Pipes: Although Pi recorded only 3 bash tool errors (an elixir -e BadMapError at line 19, a 30s timeout on a backgrounded sleep 30 signal test at line 76, and an ungrouped defp run_target/1 compiler warning at line 513), the agent actually executed 48 bash commands that produced compiler errors, test failures, or exceptions—including all deliberate TDD red-phase test runs (lines 57, 94, 137, 255, 350, 391, 431). Because the agent habitually piped commands through 2>&1 | tail -n ... or 2>&1 | head -n ... without pipefail, POSIX sh returned tail/head's exit code 0.

Four Silent erl_crash.dump Files & the S1 git commit --amend (Lines 18–20, 32–34, 85–88, 250–252): Two early erl -eval one-liners calling non-existent os:get_signal/1 (line 18) and os:signal_support/0 (line 32) crashed during boot, and piping mix help escript.build 2>&1 | head -n 60 (line 50) plus S3 test output through head closed stdout early on the BEAM—generating erl_crash.dump four times. At line 85, running git add -A for the S1 commit accidentally staged both erl_crash.dump and records/2026-10-25T22-32-50-647Z_01a17531-f4d6-716e-b04f-0e05a07345e9.jsonl; the agent immediately caught this in the git status output and amended commit 9a2f0f9 at line 87 before adding /erl_crash.dump and /records/ to .gitignore in S4 (lines 251 & 346).
